To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the physiological responses of intact photoreceptor axons that are isolated from their synapses are indistinguishable, at moderate light intensities, from those of normal photoreceptor cells.

(i) the receptor potentials of intact photoreceptors lacking synapses are identical to those of normal photoreceptors; (ii) the receptor potentials spread electrotonically into axons without initiating spikes; (iii) the transplants adapt in a normal manner; (iv) the transplants are capable of responding to a variety of light stimuli; and (v) the transplants have no synapses with higher-order neurons.

the electrical responses of isolated photoreceptor cells are identical to those of normal photoreceptor cells, and that the development of the optic lobe does not appear to be necessary for normal development of photoreceptor cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of the visual system of insects.
the development of the eye of the housefly, Musca domestica.
the physiology of intact photoreceptors that lack synapses with the central nervous sys-tem.

the synaptic connections between photoreceptors and the central nervous system are not essential for the normal development of the electrical response of photoreceptor cells.

the receptor potentials are generated by the photoreceptor membrane itself.
